questions.problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}={x}_{4}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}={x}_{4}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =2(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x-2) & =2({x}^{2}-4x+4)({x}^{2}-4x+4) \\  & =2({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+16{x}^{2}-16x+4{x}^{2}-16x+16) \\  & =2({x}^{4}-8{x}^{3}+24{x}^{2}-32x+16) \\  & =2{x}^{4}-16{x}^{3}+48{x}^{2}-64x+32.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{4}-16{x}^{3}+48{x}^{2}-64x+32.$

questions.problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=1,{x}_{2}=2,{x}_{3}=-4$ and ${x}_{4}=4$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=1,{x}_{2}=2,$ ${x}_{3}=-4,$ and ${x}_{4}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-1)(x-2)(x-(-4))(x-4) \\  & =(x-1)(x-2)(x+4)(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)(x-2)(x+4)(x-4) & =({x}^{2}-3x+2)({x}^{2}-16) \\  & ={x}^{4}-16{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3}+48x+2{x}^{2}-32 \\  & ={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-14{x}^{2}+48x-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-14{x}^{2}+48x-32.$

questions.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-2,$ and ${x}_{4}=5,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-(-2))(x-(-2))(x-(-2))(x-5) \\  & =(x+2)(x+2)(x+2)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)(x+2)(x+2)(x-5) & =({x}^{2}+4x+4)({x}^{2}-3x-10) \\  & ={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-10{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-40x+4{x}^{2}-12x-40 \\  & ={x}^{4}+{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}-52x-40.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-1,$ and ${x}_{4}=3$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $2.$ Determine the **expanded form** of $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,6$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-1,$ and ${x}_{4}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =2(x-(-1))(x-(-1))(x-(-1))(x-3) \\  & =2(x+1)(x+1)(x+1)(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x+1)(x+1)(x-3) & =2({x}^{2}+2x+1)({x}^{2}-2x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-6x+{x}^{2}-2x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{4}-0{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-8x-3) \\  & =2{x}^{4}-12{x}^{2}-16x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{4}-12{x}^{2}-16x-6.$

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,$ ${x}_{2}=4,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1(x-(-1))(x-4)(x-(-2\text{i}))(x-(2\text{i})) \\  & =1(x+1)(x-4)(x+2\text{i})(x-2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)(x-4)(x+2\text{i})(x-2\text{i}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}+x-4x-4)({x}^{2}+(2\text{i}-2\text{i})x-(2\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-3x-4)({x}^{2}+4) & = \\ {x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3}-12x-4{x}^{2}-16 & = \\ {x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-12x-16 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-12x-16.$

canonical_examples.problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots $x_1=0, x_2=-1,x_3=2$ and $x_4=-3,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $4.$ Find $P(x).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x_1=0, x_2=-1},$ ${x_3=2},$ and ${x_4=-3},$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is ${a=4},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =4(x-0)(x-(-1))(x-2)(x-(-3)) \\  & =4(x-0)(x+1)(x-2)(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x-0)(x+1)(x-2)(x+3) & =4({x}^{2}+x)({x}^{2}+x-6) \\  & =4({x}^{4}+{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-6x) \\  & =4({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}-6x) \\  & =4{x}^{4}+8{x}^{3}-20{x}^{2}-24x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = 4x^4+8x^3-20x^2-24x.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x_1=-2},$ ${x_2=3},$ and ${x_{3,4}=1 \pm 3\textrm{i}}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is ${a=1}.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1\cdot (x-(-2))(x-(3))(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i})) \\  & =(x+2)(x-3)(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)(x-3)(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i})) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-3x+2x-6)({x}^{2}-x(1-3\text{i})-x(1+3\text{i})+(1+3\text{i})(1-3\text{i})) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-x-6)({x}^{2}-2x+10) & = \\ {x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+10{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-10x-6{x}^{2}+12x-60 & = \\ {x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+2x-60 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x) = x^4 - 3x^3 + 6x^2 + 2x - 60.$
